liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments rose by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}, taking cash liquidity to revenue up by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}.

Customer prepayments grew: contract liabilities rose by {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2025}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2025}}, and advance ticket cover increased by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2025}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}}.

The funding profile carries a downgrade: Fitch cut the company to a lower rating with a stable outlook during the year, citing slower capacity growth from the engine issues, leverage above the threshold for an investment-grade rating and higher costs.

snapshot.text: Wizz Air, the low-cost carrier operating an all-Airbus narrowbody fleet, closed FY2025 with revenue up {{revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{revenue@FY2025}} while a manufacturer engine recall kept a large part of the fleet grounded through the year.
The EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}, and net leverage rose by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{net_leverage@FY2025}}.

The point to watch is leverage: net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2025}} sits well above the peer median of {{net_leverage.peer_median@FY2025}}, and Fitch downgraded the company during the year, citing slower capacity growth from the engine issues.
